description: Restore plugin states to exactly match a previously saved snapshot.

snapshot.description: A snapshot dict as returned by :meth:`save_snapshot`, containing at minimum a ``"plugins"`` key with a list of ``folderName`` values for the plugins that should be enabled. All other plugins will be disabled.

bulk.description: When ``True`` (default), all enable and disable changes are sent in a single PATCH request. When ``False``, one PATCH request is made per plugin change.

examples.user_query: Restore the plugin configuration to match the snapshot we saved earlier.
examples.notes: This call restores the plugin state to match the provided snapshot, enabling 'data_connector_v2', 'custom_theme_manager', and 'audit_logger' while disabling all other plugins. Changes are sent in a single PATCH request for efficiency.

examples.user_query: Apply a snapshot to enable only the 'geo_visualization' plugin and disable everything else, but send changes one at a time.
examples.notes: This call enables the 'geo_visualization' plugin and disables all others, sending one PATCH request per plugin change. Use this mode if you need granular control or error handling for each change.

examples.user_query: Revert the plugins to a snapshot that includes 'data_exporter' and 'advanced_charts', ensuring all other plugins are turned off.
examples.notes: This call restores the plugin state to enable 'data_exporter' and 'advanced_charts' while disabling all other plugins. Changes are sent in a single PATCH request for faster execution.

description: Capture the current plugin enable/disable state as a snapshot.

examples.user_query: How can I save the current state of enabled plugins so I can restore it later?
examples.notes: This call captures the current enable/disable state of all plugins as a snapshot. Use this when you want to save the current plugin configuration for future restoration.

examples.user_query: I need to back up the current plugin configuration before making changes. How do I do that?
examples.notes: This call creates a snapshot of the current plugin state. It's useful for creating a backup before enabling or disabling plugins.

examples.user_query: Can I save the current plugin setup to ensure I can revert to it later if needed?
examples.notes: This call saves the current state of enabled plugins. Use it to ensure you can revert to the same configuration after making changes.
